questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following thermodynamic quantities is an exact differential for a closed, single-phase system of constant composition?
questions.explanationEn: Heat ($\delta q_{\text{rev}}$) and work ($\delta w_{\text{rev}} = -P\,dV$) are path functions and therefore inexact differentials. According to the Second Law of Thermodynamics, multiplying $\delta q_{\text{rev}}$ by the integrating factor $1/T$ produces $dS = \delta q_{\text{rev}}/T$, which is an exact differential of the state function entropy $S$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: One mole of an ideal gas initially at $(P_1, V_1, T_1)$ is expanded reversibly to the same final volume $V_2 = 2V_1$ along two different paths: Path I is isothermal and Path II is adiabatic. Which of the following inequalities is CORRECT?
questions.explanationEn: In an adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas, temperature drops ($T_{2,\text{II}} < T_1 = T_{2,\text{I}}$) because work is done at the expense of internal energy. Since both paths reach the same $V_2$, the ideal gas law gives $P_{2,\text{I}} > P_{2,\text{II}}$. Consequently, the adiabatic $P$-$V$ curve lies strictly below the isotherm, so the area under the curve ($|w|$) satisfies $|w_{\text{I}}| > |w_{\text{II}}|$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A binary liquid mixture of acetone and chloroform exhibits strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding between unlike molecules. Which of the following features is observed for this mixture?
optionsEn: Negative deviation from Raoult's law and a maximum-boiling azeotrope
Positive deviation from Raoult's law and a minimum-boiling azeotrope
Negative deviation from Raoult's law and a minimum-boiling azeotrope
questions.explanationEn: Strong hydrogen bonding between the carbonyl oxygen of acetone and the acidic $\text{C}-\text{H}$ proton of chloroform makes $\text{A}-\text{B}$ interactions stronger than $\text{A}-\text{A}$ and $\text{B}-\text{B}$ interactions. This lowers the escaping tendency (vapor pressure) below Raoult's law (negative deviation, $\Delta_{\text{mix}} H < 0$) and produces a maximum-boiling azeotrope.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the one-component sulfur phase diagram (containing rhombic sulfur, monoclinic sulfur, liquid sulfur, and sulfur vapor), the maximum number of phases that can coexist simultaneously in equilibrium is:
questions.explanationEn: By the Gibbs phase rule $F = C - P + 2$. For a single-component system ($C = 1$), $F = 3 - P$. Since the number of degrees of freedom $F$ cannot be negative ($F \ge 0$), the maximum number of coexisting phases is $P_{\max} = 3$ (occurring at invariant triple points, where $F = 0$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a two-component solid-liquid phase diagram, a solid compound $\text{AB}_2$ decomposes upon heating at a specific temperature $T_p$ into solid $\text{B}$ and a liquid of composition different from $\text{AB}_2$. This phenomenon is known as:
optionsEn: Congruent melting at a dystectic point
Incongruent melting at a peritectic point
questions.explanationEn: When an intermediate solid compound decomposes reversibly on heating into a different solid phase and a liquid phase of another composition ($\text{AB}_2(\text{s}) \rightleftharpoons \text{B}(\text{s}) + \text{Liquid}$), the process is called incongruent melting and the invariant decomposition temperature $T_p$ is the peritectic point.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following thermodynamic properties are intensive?
questions.explanationEn: An intensive property is independent of the mass or extent of the system. Chemical potential $\mu_i = (\partial G/\partial n_i)_{T,P}$, molar Gibbs energy $G_m = G/n$, and isothermal compressibility $\kappa_T = -\frac{1}{V}(\partial V/\partial P)_T$ are all intensive. Total heat capacity $C_p$ scales linearly with mass/moles and is extensive.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a binary liquid solution of volatile solvent $A$ and dilute volatile solute $B$, which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?
optionsEn: As $x_B \to 0$, the solvent $A$ obeys Raoult's law.
As $x_B \to 0$, the solute $B$ obeys Henry's law.
If the solution is ideal over the entire composition range, the Henry's law constant $K_{H,B}$ equals the pure vapor pressure $P_B^\circ$.
Henry's law constant $K_{H,B}$ is always strictly equal to $P_B^\circ$ even for non-ideal solutions.
questions.explanationEn: In any sufficiently dilute solution ($x_B \to 0$, $x_A \to 1$), the solvent obeys Raoult's law ($P_A = x_A P_A^\circ$) and by the Gibbs-Duhem relation the solute obeys Henry's law ($P_B = x_B K_{H,B}$). For a completely ideal solution, $K_{H,B} = P_B^\circ$, whereas for non-ideal solutions $K_{H,B}$ differs from $P_B^\circ$ (so D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Two moles of an ideal gas expand isothermally and reversibly from $5.0\text{ L}$ to $20.0\text{ L}$ at $300\text{ K}$. The work done on the gas ($w$, in $\text{kJ}$, rounded off to two decimal places) is _______. (Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.explanationEn: For an isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gas, $w = -nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$. Substituting $n = 2.0\text{ mol}$, $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, $T = 300\text{ K}$, and $V_2/V_1 = 20.0/5.0 = 4$: $w = -2.0 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \ln(4) = -4988.4 \times 1.38629 = -6915.4\text{ J} = -6.92\text{ kJ}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A reversible Carnot heat engine absorbs $500\text{ J}$ of heat from a hot reservoir at $700\text{ K}$ and rejects heat to a cold reservoir at $280\text{ K}$. The magnitude of net work performed by the engine per cycle (in $\text{J}$, in integer) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The Carnot efficiency is $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_c}{T_h} = 1 - \frac{280}{700} = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$. The magnitude of net work performed per cycle is $|w| = \eta q_h = 0.6 \times 500\text{ J} = 300\text{ J}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a simple binary eutectic system of components $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ (with no solid solubility), $10.0\text{ mol}$ of an overall mixture with $x_{\text{B}} = 0.35$ is cooled to a temperature where pure solid $\text{A}$ ($x_{\text{B}} = 0$) is in equilibrium with a liquid phase of composition $x_{\text{B}} = 0.50$. The total number of moles of the liquid phase present at this temperature (rounded off to one decimal place) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Applying the lever rule between pure solid $\text{A}$ ($x_{\text{B,s}} = 0$) and the liquid phase ($x_{\text{B,l}} = 0.50$) for overall composition $x_{\text{B}} = 0.35$: $\frac{n_{\text{l}}}{n_{\text{total}}} = \frac{x_{\text{B}} - x_{\text{B,s}}}{x_{\text{B,l}} - x_{\text{B,s}}} = \frac{0.35 - 0}{0.50 - 0} = 0.70$. Thus, $n_{\text{l}} = 0.70 \times 10.0 = 7.0\text{ mol}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a real gas obeying the equation of state $P(V_m - b) = RT$ (where $b$ is a positive constant), the value of $\left(\frac{\partial H_m}{\partial P}\right)_T$ and the sign of its Joule-Thomson coefficient $\mu_{\text{JT}}$ are, respectively:
questions.explanationEn: From the thermodynamic equation of state for enthalpy, $\left(\frac{\partial H_m}{\partial P}\right)_T = V_m - T\left(\frac{\partial V_m}{\partial T}\right)_P$. Since $V_m = \frac{RT}{P} + b$, we have $\left(\frac{\partial V_m}{\partial T}\right)_P = \frac{R}{P}$, so $\left(\frac{\partial H_m}{\partial P}\right)_T = \left(\frac{RT}{P} + b\right) - T\left(\frac{R}{P}\right) = b > 0$. Because $\mu_{\text{JT}} = -\frac{1}{C_{p,m}}\left(\frac{\partial H_m}{\partial P}\right)_T = -\frac{b}{C_{p,m}} < 0$, the gas warms upon throttling expansion.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Liquids $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ form an ideal solution at $300\text{ K}$ with pure vapor pressures $P_A^\circ = 100\text{ kPa}$ and $P_B^\circ = 40\text{ kPa}$. For an equimolar liquid mixture ($x_A = x_B = 0.50$), the mole fraction of $\text{A}$ in the equilibrium vapor phase ($y_A$) is:
questions.explanationEn: By Raoult's law, $P_A = x_A P_A^\circ = 0.50 \times 100 = 50\text{ kPa}$ and $P_B = x_B P_B^\circ = 0.50 \times 40 = 20\text{ kPa}$, giving total vapor pressure $P_{\text{total}} = 50 + 20 = 70\text{ kPa}$. By Dalton's law, the mole fraction of $\text{A}$ in the vapor is $y_A = \frac{P_A}{P_{\text{total}}} = \frac{50}{70} = \frac{5}{7}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: One mole of a van der Waals gas undergoes an adiabatic free expansion into a vacuum from volume $V_1$ to $V_2$ ($V_2 > V_1$). Assuming constant $C_{V,m}$, the temperature change $\Delta T = T_2 - T_1$ is:
questions.explanationEn: In an adiabatic free expansion, $q = 0$ and $w = 0$, so $\Delta U_m = 0$. Using $dU_m = C_{V,m}\,dT + \left(\frac{\partial U_m}{\partial V_m}\right)_T dV_m = 0$ and $\left(\frac{\partial U_m}{\partial V_m}\right)_T = \frac{a}{V_m^2}$ for a van der Waals gas: $C_{V,m}\Delta T = -\int_{V_1}^{V_2} \frac{a}{V_m^2}\,dV_m = a\left(\frac{1}{V_2} - \frac{1}{V_1}\right)$. Since $V_2 > V_1$, $\Delta T < 0$ (cooling), giving $\Delta T = \frac{a}{C_{V,m}}\left(\frac{1}{V_2} - \frac{1}{V_1}\right)$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: At a fixed pressure $P$, the chemical potential $\mu$ of a pure substance is plotted against temperature $T$ for the solid, liquid, and gas phases. Which statement correctly describes the slopes and relative positions of these curves?
optionsEn: All three curves have positive slopes, with gas having the steepest positive slope.
The curves are concave upward ($\partial^2 \mu/\partial T^2 > 0$) because $C_{p,m} > 0$.
All three curves have negative slopes, with $|\text{slope}_{\text{solid}}| > |\text{slope}_{\text{liquid}}| > |\text{slope}_{\text{gas}}|$, and the stable phase has the highest $\mu$.
All three curves have negative slopes, with $|\text{slope}_{\text{gas}}| > |\text{slope}_{\text{liquid}}| > |\text{slope}_{\text{solid}}|$, and the stable phase at any $T$ has the lowest $\mu$.
questions.explanationEn: Since $\left(\frac{\partial \mu}{\partial T}\right)_P = -S_m < 0$, all three $\mu(T)$ curves slope downward, and because $S_{m,\text{gas}} > S_{m,\text{liquid}} > S_{m,\text{solid}}$, the gas curve is steepest and the solid curve is shallowest. At constant $T$ and $P$, the thermodynamically stable phase minimizes $\mu$. Moreover, $(\partial^2 \mu/\partial T^2)_P = -C_{p,m}/T < 0$, so the curves are concave downward.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Benzoic acid undergoes partial dimerization in benzene according to $2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH} \rightleftharpoons (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH})_2$ with degree of association $\alpha$. If $M_{\text{calc}}$ is the true molar mass and $M_{\text{obs}}$ is the apparent molar mass determined from freezing point depression, then $\alpha$ is equal to:
questions.explanationEn: For dimerization ($n = 2$), $1\text{ mol}$ of solute yields $(1 - \alpha) + \frac{\alpha}{2} = 1 - \frac{\alpha}{2}$ moles of particles in solution, so the van't Hoff factor is $i = 1 - \frac{\alpha}{2}$. Since colligative properties are inversely proportional to apparent molar mass, $i = \frac{M_{\text{calc}}}{M_{\text{obs}}}$. Equating gives $1 - \frac{\alpha}{2} = \frac{M_{\text{calc}}}{M_{\text{obs}}} \implies \alpha = 2\left(1 - \frac{M_{\text{calc}}}{M_{\text{obs}}}\right)$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following thermodynamic relations is/are ALWAYS valid for a closed, single-phase system of fixed composition undergoing reversible $P$-$V$ work only?
optionsEn: $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial V}\right)_T = P - T\left(\frac{\partial P}{\partial T}\right)_V$
questions.explanationEn: Options (A), (B), and (C) are the exact Maxwell relations derived from $dU = TdS - PdV$, $dH = TdS + VdP$, and $dG = -SdT + VdP$, respectively. Option (D) has the reversed sign: the correct thermodynamic equation of state is $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial V}\right)_T = T\left(\frac{\partial P}{\partial T}\right)_V - P$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following approximations are used to derive the Clausius-Clapeyron equation $\frac{d\ln P}{dT} = \frac{\Delta_{\text{vap}} H_m}{RT^2}$ from the exact Clapeyron equation $\frac{dP}{dT} = \frac{\Delta_{\text{vap}} H_m}{T(V_{m,\text{g}} - V_{m,\text{l}})}$?
optionsEn: The molar volume of the liquid phase is negligible compared to that of the vapor phase ($V_{m,\text{l}} \ll V_{m,\text{g}}$).
The vapor behaves as an ideal gas ($V_{m,\text{g}} = RT/P$).
The molar enthalpy of vaporization $\Delta_{\text{vap}} H_m$ is independent of temperature.
The transition occurs at the critical point.
questions.explanationEn: To obtain the differential Clausius-Clapeyron form $\frac{d\ln P}{dT} = \frac{\Delta_{\text{vap}} H_m}{RT^2}$, only two approximations are required: (1) $V_{m,\text{l}} \ll V_{m,\text{g}}$ so $\Delta V_m \approx V_{m,\text{g}}$ (A), and (2) ideal vapor $V_{m,\text{g}} = RT/P$ (B). Constant $\Delta_{\text{vap}} H_m$ (C) is an additional assumption only needed when integrating the equation; the approximation breaks down completely near the critical point where $V_{m,\text{l}} \to V_{m,\text{g}}$ (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a binary liquid-vapor system of two volatile components $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ at constant pressure, which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?
optionsEn: By Konowaloff's rule, the equilibrium vapor is always richer than the liquid in the component whose addition increases the total vapor pressure (the more volatile component).
At an azeotropic point, the liquid and vapor phases have identical compositions ($x_A = y_A$).
Azeotropic mixtures can be completely separated into pure $\text{A}$ and pure $\text{B}$ by simple fractional distillation at the same pressure.
In a $T$-$x$ diagram at constant pressure, the dew-point curve lies above the bubble-point curve.
questions.explanationEn: Konowaloff's rule states that the vapor is enriched in the component that increases total vapor pressure (A). At an azeotrope, $x_A = y_A$ (B), so fractional distillation at that pressure cannot cross the azeotropic composition to yield both pure components (C is false). In a $T$-$x$ diagram, the vapor phase is stable at higher $T$ and the liquid at lower $T$, so the dew-point (vapor) curve lies above the bubble-point (liquid) curve (D).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: One mole of an ideal diatomic gas with $C_{p,m} = \frac{7}{2}R$ is taken from $(300\text{ K},\; 1.0\text{ bar})$ to $(600\text{ K},\; 4.0\text{ bar})$. The molar entropy change ($\Delta S_m$, in $\text{J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, rounded off to two decimal places) is _______. (Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.explanationEn: Using $\Delta S_m = C_{p,m}\ln(T_2/T_1) - R\ln(P_2/P_1) = \frac{7}{2}R\ln(2) - R\ln(4) = R\left(\frac{7}{2}\ln 2 - 2\ln 2\right) = \frac{3}{2}R\ln 2 = 1.5 \times 8.314 \times 0.69315 = 8.64\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Dissolving $5.0\text{ g}$ of a synthetic polymer in $500\text{ mL}$ of toluene at $300\text{ K}$ produces an osmotic pressure of $1.2471\text{ kPa}$. Assuming ideal dilute solution behavior, the molar mass of the polymer (in $\text{kg mol}^{-1}$, rounded off to one decimal place) is _______. (Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.explanationEn: Using the van't Hoff equation $\Pi = \frac{w_2}{M_2 V} RT$, with $w_2 = 5.0\text{ g}$, $V = 500\text{ mL} = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^3$, and $\Pi = 1247.1\text{ Pa}$: $M_2 = \frac{5.0 \times 8.314 \times 300}{1247.1 \times 5.0 \times 10^{-4}} = 20000\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 20.0\text{ kg mol}^{-1}$.
